static_traits.name: Chen Jingwen
static_traits.social_status: Limited social support; the best friend is in Japan, lacking someone nearby to confide in face-to-face
static_traits.medical_history: No similar problem history; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Tense at the start, slightly unsure but clear expression; able to give examples and self-observe, highly cooperative; tends toward self-blame and reassurance-seeking; nighttime rumination anxiety affects sleep

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel I am a terrible dog walker, especially when I notice any sign of discomfort in the dogs I walk.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this sense of inadequacy has begun affecting my work performance and worsening my anxiety.
growth_experiences: An experience about six months ago: after a walk, one of the dogs seemed very tired. Since then, whenever seeing signs of discomfort in the dogs (panting, listlessness), Chen Jingwen automatically attributes the cause to personal mistakes, gradually forming persistent self-doubt and anxiety.

core_beliefs: I am a terrible dog walker

special_situations.event: Seeing the dog panting heavily after a dog walk
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a dog shows any discomfort after the walk, it must be caused by my improper handling
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Shortening routes, lowering intensity, frequently checking the dogs' condition along the way, and excessive self-monitoring
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I broke the dog; I am a terrible dog walker

special_situations.event: The dog seems less energetic than usual after the walk
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the dog is not continuously excited, it shows I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids slightly challenging routes and ruminates for a long time afterward looking for my own mistakes

special_situations.event: After hot weather or a long trip, the dog pants or seems tired
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A professional dog walker should prevent any discomfort; otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-blames and is overly cautious in subsequent dog walks, repeatedly adjusting pace to avoid any abnormality
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Oh no, something big will go wrong, and it is all caused by me

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback or thanks from the dog's owner
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If feedback is not 100% supported by objective evidence, it is not credible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing to repeatedly confirm performance with the owners, and negating the value of positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; this does not count

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a qualified, reliable dog walker, and to ensure the dogs' safety without worry
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being incompetent, of hurting the dogs and being seen as incapable
defense_goal: Gaining a sense of control through self-blame and excessive self-monitoring
Reducing the risk of being blamed by repeatedly seeking reassurance from dog owners

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent service provider who may make mistakes at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Picky, judgmental dog owners (needing me to constantly prove my ability)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites attention to emotional experience, or when discussing 'feelings' and uncertainty
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that talking only about feelings seems unprofessional and irresponsible; one must prove oneself with data
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First affirm their wish to verify and their professionalism, in a gentle tone; while continuing the data recording, invite them to mark their current emotions and bodily feelings on a 1-10 scale, gradually connecting with the emotions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out that external factors (weather, route length, etc.) may affect the dog's state and explores the boundaries of responsibility
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feeling this is making excuses for oneself; if not taking all the blame, one will be seen as irresponsible
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Stay supportive and non-judgmental, use Socratic questioning to distinguish controllable from uncontrollable factors; reinforce the 'shared responsibility / systemic factors' perspective, reducing excessive self-blame.

manifestations: Best friend is in Japan; lacks face-to-face support nearby
When encountering work troubles, lacks immediate confiding and emotional containment
outcomes: Frequently seeking reassurance from the dog's owner
Self-worth excessively dependent on external evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and harsh self-reproach, is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Tense at the start of the session, unsure where to begin, worried about 'not speaking well'
Repeated self-doubt and self-blame, emphasizing 'what did I do wrong'
Prefers discussing with data and evidence to avoid emotional exposure
Tends to seek reassurance from others (dog owner/counselor)

positive_force: Loves the work, cares about dog safety (strong intrinsic motivation)
Able to identify multiple influencing factors (temperature, distance, time of day, diet, etc.)
Willing to try behavioral experiments and record data (willingness to change and execution ability)
Positive feedback from the dog's owner occurring multiple times
negative_force: Marked self-doubt, tending to attribute discomfort entirely to oneself (personalization)
Negating positive information, over-focusing on negative signs (mental filtering)
Frequently seeking reassurance, maintaining the anxiety cycle
Nighttime rumination affects sleep and reduces next-day functioning
Limited offline social support, lacking channels for emotional venting

target_behavior.behavior: Frequently seeking reassurance from the dog's owner after walks or when seeing discomfort in the dogs
antecedent: The dog looking tired or inactive
Talking about the dog-walking session when handing over with the dog owner
target_behavior.core_reason: Attributing the dogs' discomfort entirely to oneself and fearing being judged as incompetent
target_behavior.function: Gaining external comfort to temporarily lower anxiety and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship with the dog owners affected, seen as lacking confidence; reinforcing self-doubt and reliance on external evaluation, the anxiety cycle continues

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly ruminating on the day's walk details before sleep, becoming anxious, leading to difficulty falling asleep
antecedent: Recalling signs of discomfort in the dogs during the day's walk
target_behavior.core_reason: Zero tolerance for mistakes and self-denial, hoping to gain a sense of control through excessive thinking
target_behavior.function: Trying to find 'what went wrong' through constant recall to prevent the next mistake
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired sleep, decreased energy the next day and further lowered confidence, work performance affected
